name: Omega Centauri
tagline: The largest globular cluster in the Milky Way — possibly the stripped core of a devoured galaxy.
history: Omega Centauri crowds ten million ancient stars into a sphere 150 light-years wide — the biggest and brightest globular in our sky, visible to the naked eye as a fuzzy 'star.' Its mixed stellar ages and a suspected intermediate-mass black hole at its heart suggest it is no ordinary cluster but the stripped nucleus of a dwarf galaxy the Milky Way consumed — a fossil of galactic cannibalism still circling us.
